description: concept-inbox (ADR 0031, ADR 0012): submitting a suggestion set is one function call, the set's summary is re-rendered against concept_identity every time it is asked for, and nothing reads a payload but the acceptance path. Each suite seeds `workspaces` and `concepts`, calls submit_suggestion_set as `set.role` inside a transaction scoped to `set.workspace_id`, then reads suggestion_set_summary as app_rt in that scope and asserts one row per `expect_summary` entry, in that order. Every `refusals` entry is then run as its own role, in the named scope ('' = no scope), and must fail with the SQLSTATE given — never a value.

requests.title: Expenses
requests.body: Expenses are claimed within sixty days.

requests.title: Expenses, restated
requests.body: Expenses are claimed within ninety days.

requests.title: Travel
requests.body: Travel is booked fourteen days ahead.

expect_summary.why: the merge key resolves to the concept it names, and the payload was written against the content that concept still holds
the same merge key resolves the same way, and this payload was written against content that has moved since
a merge key no concept holds is a new concept, and its acceptance mints the IRI

refusals.why: a payload is platform state in no knowledge layer: the app reaches it through the acceptance path's function and never through the table
no run reads another run's candidates out of the inbox: the payload function is the app's alone
the queue is the app's; a producer submits and reads nothing back
the summary is a decision surface, and deciding is not a producer's act
a decided suggestion is a fact, so the app has no road to a deleted one
the set lands in the workspace the caller's transaction already names, and an unscoped caller has none
